title: Sep 29 Results + Sep 30 Preview: Three Wins, One Bad Beat, Zero Apologies
summary: 75% accuracy on Sep 29, Braves feast continues tomorrow

content.value:
## Let Me Be Honest About Yesterday

Three wins out of four picks. 75% accuracy. Most people would be thrilled. Most people would write some self-congratulatory nonsense about "trusting the process." But let me tell you what really happened on September 29th—we absolutely crushed it where it mattered, and took one punch to the gut that stings more than it should.

## The Brutal Truth About Yesterday's Slate

The Braves showed up like we said they would—61% confidence, money in the bank. The Yankees took care of business against the Sox because, well, they're the Yankees. The Padres at 63%? That was our strongest conviction play and it hit like a freight train.

But that Astros pick? That 50% coin flip that went south? Here's the controversial take: **we should've never made that pick in the first place.** When you're at 50%, you're essentially admitting you have no edge. That's not handicapping, that's guessing with extra steps.

## Tomorrow's Play: The Braves Aren't Done Feasting

Here's where I'm going to make enemies: **the Phillies are cooked, and we're riding the Braves again.**

Philadelphia sends out Cristopher Sánchez, who's been solid but not spectacular. Atlanta counters with Tyler Mahle. The model sees this at 61% for the Braves—the exact same confidence we had yesterday when they delivered.

Some of you are thinking "don't chase yesterday's winner." Wrong. That's results-oriented thinking. The matchup is what matters, and this matchup screams Atlanta. The Phillies' offense has been inconsistent, their bullpen is showing cracks, and they're walking into a buzzsaw in Atlanta.

The hot take? **The Braves might be the safest play on the entire Sep 30 slate.** Not the highest upside, not the sexiest narrative, but the most likely to print money.

## The Bottom Line

We went 3-1 yesterday. We're backing the Braves again tomorrow at the same 61% confidence. If that sounds repetitive, good—consistency is how you win long-term.

The controversial truth nobody wants to hear: betting favorites with slight edges is boring, unglamorous, and profitable. Chasing underdogs for the narrative is exciting, Twitter-friendly, and broke.

See you after the Braves cash again.

— Rico
